rules.text: Each platform's shaders are compiled to a format its SDL_GPU backend accepts: SPIR-V for Vulkan, DXBC or DXIL for Direct3D 12, MSL or a metallib for Metal.
The resource counts in each SDL_GPUShaderCreateInfo (samplers, storage textures, storage buffers, uniform buffers) come from reflecting the shader, not from constants in glue.

probes.check: am_probe_shadercross_sdl3(): am_shadercross_format_for() names a format each of SDL_GPU's Vulkan, Direct3D 12 and Metal backends takes, and a test fragment shader compiled from SPIR-V for this platform's device is created on it.

seeded_violation.description: Compile to SPIR-V for every backend, as on the Vulkan development machine.

probes.check: am_probe_shadercross_sdl3(): the test shader, with one sampler and one uniform buffer, was created with the counts SDL_ShaderCross_ReflectGraphicsSPIRV reads from it.

seeded_violation.description: Set the counts to one sampler and no uniform buffers, as the engine's first shaders needed.

adaptation_notes: am_shadercross_create_shader() reflects SPIR-V, compiles it to the format am_shadercross_format_for() gives for the device's driver (SDL_GetGPUDeviceDriver), and creates the shader with the reflected resource counts.

Direct3D 12 gets DXBC, compiled through the system's d3dcompiler_47.dll, so a game needs no DXC at runtime; a game that wants DXIL (shader model 6) changes the format and ships dxcompiler.dll and dxil.dll beside the executable.
Metal reserves the name main: SPIRV-Cross renames a main entry point to main0, which the glue passes on.

Shaders a build step cooks ahead of time (the assets binding) follow the same choice of format per backend; the game then loads the cooked shader for its driver and creates it with the counts reflected at cooking time.
